definitions.explanation: Hiraga Gennai (1728–1780), a mid-Edo-period scholar of Western learning and natural history, inventor, painter and writer. He is remembered for building a working エレキテル (an electrostatic generator) and is popularly credited with starting the custom of eating eel on the Day of the Ox in midsummer.

notes:
Often called {源内|げんない} for short, and sometimes described as Japan's Leonardo da Vinci for the range of his interests.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- He studied ⟦{蘭学|らんがく}→蘭学：32987_rangaku⟧ (Western learning through Dutch books) and natural history in Nagasaki and Edo.
- His エレキテル, a friction generator rebuilt from a broken Dutch one, is his best-known invention.
- The story that he wrote a sign telling an eel shop to advertise for ⟦{土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ}→土用の丑の日：33886_doyounoushinohi⟧ is a legend, but it is the standard explanation of the custom.
- He also wrote comic fiction and plays, and painted in the Western style.
